summary: This note is a biographical entry on John Samuel Forrest, covering his education at Hamilton Academy and the University of Glasgow. It describes his school medals, the 1925 University of Glasgow Bursary Examination result that won him the John Clerk (Mile End) Bursary, and his research student status and scholarships from 1929. It ends with his 1930 graduation with a B.Sc. and second class honours.
one_line: Biographical note on John Samuel Forrest's school honours, University of Glasgow bursary and scholarships, and 1930 graduation.
key_facts: John Samuel Forrest attended the Hamilton Academy school.
At Hamilton Academy, John Samuel Forrest won the Dux Medal, the Mathematics Medal and the Science Medal.
John Samuel Forrest came third in the University of Glasgow Bursary Examination of 1925.
John Samuel Forrest was awarded the John Clerk (Mile End) Bursary to study Mathematics and Natural Philosophy at the University of Glasgow.
In 1929, while still an under-graduate, John Samuel Forrest was admitted as a research student in the Science Faculty.
In 1929, John Samuel Forrest was awarded the Thomson Experimental Scholarship.
John Samuel Forrest was later awarded the Mackay-Smith Scholarship.
John Samuel Forrest won the Thomson Prize in Astronomy.
John Samuel Forrest graduated in 1930 with a double degree.
The 1930 double degree comprised a B.Sc. in pure science.
John Samuel Forrest graduated in 1930 with second class honours in Mathematics and Natural Philosophy.
